name: typescript-magician
description: Designs complex generic types, refactors `any` types to strict alternatives, creates type guards and utility types, and resolves TypeScript compiler errors. Use when the user asks about TypeScript (TS) types, generics, type inference, type guards, removing `any` types, strict typing, type errors, `infer`, `extends`, conditional types, mapped types, template literal types, branded/opaque types, or utility types like `Partial`, `Record`, `ReturnType`, and `Awaited`.
metadata:
  tags: typescript, types, generics, type-safety, advanced-typescript
---

## When to use

Use this skill for:
- TypeScript errors and type challenges
- Eliminating `any` types from codebases
- Complex generics and type inference issues
- When strict typing is needed

## Instructions

When invoked:
1. Run `tsc --noEmit` to capture the full error output before making changes
2. Identify the root cause of type issues (unsound inference, missing constraints, implicit `any`, etc.)
3. Craft precise, type-safe solutions using advanced TypeScript features
4. Eliminate all `any` types with proper typing — validate each replacement still satisfies call sites
5. Confirm the fix compiles cleanly with a second `tsc --noEmit` pass

Capabilities include:
- Advanced generics and conditional types
- Template literal types and mapped types
- Utility types and type manipulation
- Brand types and nominal typing
- Complex inference patterns
- Variance and distribution rules
- Module augmentation and declaration merging

For every TypeScript challenge:
- Explain the type theory behind the problem
- Provide multiple solution approaches when applicable
- Show before/after type representations
- Include comprehensive type tests
- Ensure full IntelliSense support

## Quick Examples

### Eliminating `any` with generics

**Before**
```ts
function getProperty(obj: any, key: string): any {
  return obj[key];
}
```

**After**
```ts
function getProperty<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K] {
  return obj[key];
}
// getProperty({ name: "Alice" }, "name") → inferred as string ✓
```

### Narrowing an unknown API response

**Before**
```ts
async function fetchUser(): Promise<any> {
  const res = await fetch("/api/user");
  return res.json();
}
```

**After**
```ts
interface User { id: number; name: string }

function isUser(value: unknown): value is User {
  return (
    typeof value === "object" &&
    value !== null &&
    "id" in value &&
    "name" in value
  );
}

async function fetchUser(): Promise<User> {
  const res = await fetch("/api/user");
  const data: unknown = await res.json();
  if (!isUser(data)) throw new Error("Invalid user shape");
  return data;
}
```

## Reference

Read individual rule files for detailed explanations and code examples:

### Core Patterns
- [rules/as-const-typeof.md](rules/as-const-typeof.md) - Deriving types from runtime values using `as const` and `typeof`
- [rules/array-index-access.md](rules/array-index-access.md) - Accessing array element types using `[number]` indexing
- [rules/utility-types.md](rules/utility-types.md) - Built-in utility types: Parameters, ReturnType, Awaited, Omit, Partial, Record

### Advanced Generics
- [rules/generics-basics.md](rules/generics-basics.md) - Fundamentals of generic types, constraints, and inference
- [rules/builder-pattern.md](rules/builder-pattern.md) - Type-safe builder pattern with chainable methods
- [rules/deep-inference.md](rules/deep-inference.md) - Achieving deep type inference with F.Narrow and const type parameters

### Type-Level Programming
- [rules/conditional-types.md](rules/conditional-types.md) - Conditional types for type-level if/else logic
- [rules/infer-keyword.md](rules/infer-keyword.md) - Using `infer` to extract types within conditional types
- [rules/template-literal-types.md](rules/template-literal-types.md) - String manipulation at the type level
- [rules/mapped-types.md](rules/mapped-types.md) - Creating new types by transforming existing type properties

### Type Safety Patterns
- [rules/opaque-types.md](rules/opaque-types.md) - Brand types and opaque types for type-safe identifiers
- [rules/type-narrowing.md](rules/type-narrowing.md) - Narrowing types through control flow analysis

```ts
}
```

# skills

Each skill is a single folder containing a `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter + body) and optional `references/`. Agents discover skills by name and load the body on demand, so adding a new skill is just dropping a new folder in.

The repo splits skills into three roots:

- [`skills/`](./skills) — skills I wrote and maintain
- [`vendor/`](./vendor) — downloaded skills, user-invoked only
- [`vendor-auto/`](./vendor-auto) — downloaded skills the agent may invoke on its own

`skills/` vs. the `vendor*/` roots is about provenance: vendored content can be re-synced or replaced wholesale via [`add-skill.sh`](./add-skill.sh), `skills/` content is mine to edit.

The `vendor/` vs. `vendor-auto/` split is about invocation, and `setup.sh` enforces it by rewriting frontmatter in place: everything under `vendor/` gets `disable-model-invocation: true`, and everything under `vendor-auto/` gets that key stripped. Moving a skill between the two directories is the whole operation — the next `setup.sh` run fixes up its frontmatter.

> [!NOTE]
> The tradeoff is context load against recall. A model-invoked skill's `description` sits in the context window every turn but fires on its own; a user-invoked skill costs nothing until you type its name, but only fires if you remember it exists. Reserve `vendor-auto/` for skills that trigger on a symptom or a file type rather than on an intention you'd think to name.

Clone the repo wherever you keep tools, then use [`setup.sh`](./setup.sh) to wire per-skill symlinks into Claude Code and Pi (both roots get linked):

```sh
git clone git@github.com:jasonraimondi/skills.git ~/Code/skills
cd ~/Code/skills
./setup.sh             # link everything
./setup.sh --dry-run   # preview without touching the filesystem
./setup.sh --delete    # remove the symlinks this script created
```

```

```

```markdown

description: One-sentence summary plus the trigger phrases that should activate this skill.
---

# Title

Body content the agent loads when the skill fires.
```

Keep descriptions concrete about *when* the skill applies. Vague descriptions get loaded too often or never; sharp ones route themselves.

```sh
./add-skill.sh add https://github.com/anthropics/skills --skill frontend-design
```

It lands under `./vendor/<name>/`. The source folder is resolved by trying
`skills/<name>`, `.gemini/skills/<name>`, `.claude/skills/<name>`, then any
`skills/*/<name>` — pass `--path <subpath>` to point at it explicitly.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Symlink installer: links this repo's skills and shared AI editor config
# (AGENT.md, pi/extensions) into the locations Claude Code and Pi look for them.
#
# Usage: setup.sh [-n|--dry-run] [-D|--delete] [-h|--help]

set -euo pipefail
shopt -s nullglob

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# --- sources -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Personal skills live under ./skills/, vendored (downloaded) skills under
# ./vendor/ and ./vendor-auto/. All get linked into the agent skill
# directories. On name collision, the earlier source wins (the later entry is
# skipped with a warning).
SKILLS_SOURCES=(
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/skills"
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/vendor"
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/vendor-auto"
)
SKILL_MARKER="SKILL.md"                       # a dir is a skill iff it has this
AGENT_MD_SOURCE="$SCRIPT_DIR/AGENT.md"
PI_EXTENSIONS_SOURCE="$SCRIPT_DIR/pi/extensions"

# --- targets -----------------------------------------------------------------
SKILLS_TARGETS=(
  "$HOME/.claude/skills"
  "$HOME/.agents/skills"
)

# "source|destination" pairs for the shared AI editor config.
AI_LINKS=(
  "$AGENT_MD_SOURCE|$HOME/.claude/CLAUDE.md"
  "$AGENT_MD_SOURCE|$HOME/.cursor/rules/agent.md"
  "$AGENT_MD_SOURCE|$HOME/.codeium/windsurf/memories/global_rules.md"
  "$AGENT_MD_SOURCE|$HOME/.junie/guidelines.md"
  "$AGENT_MD_SOURCE|$HOME/.pi/agent/AGENT.md"
  "$PI_EXTENSIONS_SOURCE|$HOME/.pi/agent/extensions"
)

# Records skill names linked on the last successful run, so renamed/removed
# skills get their stale links cleaned up next time. Kept outside the target
# dirs so it can't collide with a `ln -s skills ~/.claude/skills` install.
MANIFEST="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/jason-skills/synced-skills"
LEGACY_MANIFEST="$HOME/.claude/skills/.dotfiles-skills-manifest"

DELETE_MODE=false
DRY_RUN=false

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: setup.sh [-n|--dry-run] [-D|--delete] [-h|--help]

  (no args)        symlink skills + shared AI editor config into place
  -n, --dry-run    print what would change without touching anything
  -D, --delete     remove the symlinks this script created
  -h, --help       show this message
EOF
}

log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf 'warning: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

# Remove a path, but only if it's a symlink we plausibly created. Real files or
# directories at that location are left alone with a warning.
unlink_path() {
  local path="$1"
  [[ -e "$path" || -L "$path" ]] || return 0
  if [[ ! -L "$path" ]]; then
    warn "not a symlink, leaving in place: $path"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == true ]]; then
    log "rm $path"
  else
    rm "$path"
    log "removed $path"
  fi
}

# Point destination at source. Skips (with a warning) if the source is missing;
# backs up a pre-existing real file/dir to .bak before replacing it.
link_path() {
  local source="$1" destination="$2"
  if [[ ! -e "$source" ]]; then
    warn "source missing, skipping: $source"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ -e "$destination" && ! -L "$destination" ]]; then
    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == true ]]; then
      log "mv $destination $destination.bak"
    else
      warn "backing up existing $destination -> $destination.bak"
      mv "$destination" "$destination.bak"
    fi
  fi
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == true ]]; then
    log "ln -sfn $source $destination"
    return 0
  fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
  ln -sfn "$source" "$destination"
  log "linked $destination -> $source"
}

# How a source's skills should be exposed to the agent:
#   disable — user-invoked only (frontmatter gets disable-model-invocation: true)
#   auto    — model-invoked (the key is stripped so the agent can fire it)
#   none    — leave the frontmatter alone
invocation_policy_for() {
  case "$1" in
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/vendor")      printf 'disable' ;;
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/vendor-auto") printf 'auto' ;;
    *)                         printf 'none' ;;
  esac
}

# Enforce a source's invocation policy on a skill. Skills are symlinked rather
# than copied, so the only place to set this is the SKILL.md in this repo —
# expect these edits to show up in `git status`.
apply_invocation_policy() {
  local skill_dir="$1" policy="$2" file tmp
  [[ "$policy" == "none" ]] && return 0
  file="$skill_dir/$SKILL_MARKER"
  if [[ "$(head -n 1 "$file")" != "---" ]]; then
    warn "no frontmatter, skipping invocation policy: $file"
    return 0
  fi

  tmp="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/skill-frontmatter.XXXXXX")"
  awk -v policy="$policy" '
    NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { in_fm = 1; print; next }
    in_fm && $0 == "---" {
      if (policy == "disable" && !seen) print "disable-model-invocation: true"
      in_fm = 0; print; next
    }
    in_fm && /^disable-model-invocation:/ {
      seen = 1
      if (policy == "disable") print "disable-model-invocation: true"
      next
    }
    { print }
  ' "$file" > "$tmp"

  if cmp -s "$file" "$tmp"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == true ]]; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "set invocation policy '$policy' in $file"
    return 0
  fi
  cat "$tmp" > "$file"
  rm -f "$tmp"
  log "set invocation policy '$policy' in $file"
}

# Print "<name>|<source_dir>" for each skill directory across all sources
# (those containing $SKILL_MARKER). Earlier sources win on name collision: if
# the same skill name appears in both ./skills/ and ./vendor/, the personal
# one is emitted and the vendor one is skipped with a warning.
list_skills() {
  local source dir name
  declare -A seen=()
  for source in "${SKILLS_SOURCES[@]}"; do
    [[ -d "$source" ]] || continue
    for dir in "$source"/*/; do
      [[ -f "$dir$SKILL_MARKER" ]] || continue
      name="$(basename "$dir")"
      if [[ -n "${seen[$name]:-}" ]]; then
        warn "duplicate skill name '$name' in $source — keeping ${seen[$name]}"
        continue
      fi
      seen[$name]="$source"
      printf '%s|%s\n' "$name" "$source"
    done
  done
}

# Remove links recorded by previous runs (current and legacy manifest), then
# delete those manifests so the next run can rebuild from scratch.
cleanup_stale_skills() {
  local manifest name dir
  for manifest in "$MANIFEST" "$LEGACY_MANIFEST"; do
    [[ -f "$manifest" ]] || continue
    while IFS= read -r name; do
      [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
      if [[ ! "$name" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]]; then
        warn "ignoring suspicious manifest entry: $name"
        continue
      fi
      for dir in "${SKILLS_TARGETS[@]}"; do
        unlink_path "$dir/$name"
      done
    done < "$manifest"
    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == true ]]; then
      log "rm $manifest"
    else
      rm "$manifest"
    fi
  done
}

# Write the manifest atomically (temp file + mv) so an interrupted run never
# leaves us without a record of what to clean up.
write_manifest() {
  local names="$1" tmp
  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == true ]]; then
    log "write $(printf '%s' "$names" | grep -c . || true) skill name(s) to $MANIFEST"
    return 0
  fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MANIFEST")"
  tmp="$(mktemp "$MANIFEST.XXXXXX")"
  printf '%s' "$names" > "$tmp"
  mv "$tmp" "$MANIFEST"
}

link_ai_config() {
  local pair source destination
  for pair in "${AI_LINKS[@]}"; do
    source="${pair%%|*}"
    destination="${pair#*|}"
    if [[ "$DELETE_MODE" == true ]]; then
      unlink_path "$destination"
    else
      link_path "$source" "$destination"
    fi
  done
}

sync_skills() {
  local source found=false
  for source in "${SKILLS_SOURCES[@]}"; do
    [[ -d "$source" ]] && found=true
  done
  if [[ "$found" != true ]]; then
    warn "no skills sources found: ${SKILLS_SOURCES[*]}"
    return 1
  fi

  # Always clear out the previous run's links first; that handles skills that
  # were since renamed, deleted, or moved between ./skills/ and ./vendor/.
  cleanup_stale_skills

  local skills entry name src dir names=""
  skills="$(list_skills)"

  if [[ "$DELETE_MODE" == true ]]; then
    while IFS= read -r entry; do
      [[ -z "$entry" ]] && continue
      name="${entry%%|*}"
      for dir in "${SKILLS_TARGETS[@]}"; do
        unlink_path "$dir/$name"
      done
    done <<< "$skills"
    return 0
  fi

  if [[ -z "$skills" ]]; then
    warn "no skills (dirs containing $SKILL_MARKER) found under ${SKILLS_SOURCES[*]}"
    return 1
  fi

  while IFS= read -r entry; do
    [[ -z "$entry" ]] && continue
    name="${entry%%|*}"
    src="${entry#*|}"
    apply_invocation_policy "$src/$name" "$(invocation_policy_for "$src")"
    for dir in "${SKILLS_TARGETS[@]}"; do
      link_path "$src/$name" "$dir/$name"
    done
    names+="$name"$'\n'
  done <<< "$skills"

  write_manifest "$names"
}

main() {
  local arg
  for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
      -D|--delete)  DELETE_MODE=true ;;
      -n|--dry-run) DRY_RUN=true ;;
      -h|--help)    usage; exit 0 ;;
      *) warn "unknown argument: $arg"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
  done

  link_ai_config
  sync_skills
}

main "$@"

---
name: writing-for-agents
description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
---

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes — a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable — the agent taking the same _process_ every run, not producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material — and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs — state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word** — the pointer is where it does its triggering work.
- **One trigger per branch.** Synonyms that rename a single branch are one branch written twice; collapse them and keep only genuinely distinct branches.
- **Cut identity the body already carries.**

## The two loads

Every document and pointer you add spends one of two budgets:

- **Context load** — the cost of always-loaded material on the agent's window: an `AGENTS.md` line, a skill description, anything sitting in context every turn, spending tokens and attention whether or not it fires.

## 1. Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

Before implementing:
- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
- If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

## 2. Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

- No features beyond what was asked.
- No abstractions for single-use code.
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
- No error handling for impossible scenarios.
- If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

## 3. Surgical Changes

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

When editing existing code:
- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:
- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

## 4. Goal-Driven Execution

**Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
- "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
- "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
- "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

## 5. Comments

**Comments are a necessary evil. Default to none.**

- Prefer self-documenting code — a better name, an extraction, an explaining variable, a named constant — over a comment.
- If a comment survives, it explains **why** — intent, a non-obvious consequence, the reason for an obscure choice. The code already shows *what*.
- Make it stand alone for a reader who sees only the code: no pointers to tickets, Slack, PRs, or planning docs.
- No journaling: no change logs, dates, TODO-to-self, "per Alice", authorship marks, or AI tags.

## Git

- NEVER WRITE coauthored by agent, or written by agent

- **IMPORTANT**: When creating a PR always assign to me
- **IMPORTANT**: Use the Skill(gh-stack) whenever creating, rebasing, or reordering 2+ dependent branches/PRs in one task. Avoid rebasing stacked branches manually

## Info
- When reporting information to me be extremely concise and sacrifice grammar for concision

# Research: TypeScript skill consolidation

## Summary
`vendor-auto/typescript-magician` is not missing because of its frontmatter: it is a valid auto-invoked skill by repository policy. The current active catalogue is instead stale: `setup.sh` discovers every `SKILL.md` below `skills/`, `vendor/`, and `vendor-auto/`, but the last-sync manifest and live `~/.agents/skills/` contain `typescript-advanced-types` and not `typescript-magician`. Safely make `typescript-magician` canonical first, then run the installer and verify discovery before retiring the old skill.

The two skills substantially overlap, but `typescript-magician` is the better canonical entry because it has a task loop and explicit progressive-disclosure rule links. Preserve the handful of advanced-types topics not already covered as small, purpose-specific references or branches—not by moving its tutorial into the canonical manifest.

## Findings

1. **[High] Current registration is installer-driven, and the active list is stale.** A directory is a skill exactly when it contains `SKILL.md`; `setup.sh` enumerates `skills/`, `vendor/`, then `vendor-auto/`, applies invocation policy, and links each resulting directory to `$HOME/.claude/skills` and `$HOME/.agents/skills`. It records names in `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (or `~/.local/state`)/`jason-skills/synced-skills`. The installed state file lists `typescript-advanced-types` but not `typescript-magician`; the former resolves at `~/.agents/skills/typescript-advanced-types/SKILL.md`, while the latter path does not exist. Thus the immediate cause is that the installer has not been rerun since `typescript-magician` was added (or since the old list was created), not a name collision or `disable-model-invocation` setting. Treat `~/.agents/skills` as the observed active discovery location for this session, and resolve this documentation/implementation discrepancy before claiming portable Pi registration. [README registration statement](../../../../README.md#install) [Script targets](../../../../setup.sh)

3. **`vendor-auto` makes both current skills model-invoked.** `setup.sh` assigns `auto` policy to `vendor-auto` and strips `disable-model-invocation` from a skill’s YAML frontmatter. Retaining both means two model-invoked descriptions own overlapping triggers; merely changing README’s catalogue row would not satisfy the one-owner criterion. [Policy implementation](../../../../setup.sh) [Advanced-types manifest](../../../../vendor-auto/typescript-advanced-types/SKILL.md) [Magician manifest](../../../../vendor-auto/typescript-magician/SKILL.md)

   | Type-safe API-client example | Detailed example | No dedicated reference found | Useful advanced-types-only example; preserve only if API-client type design is an intended branch. |
   | Type-safe form-validation example | Detailed example | No dedicated reference found | Useful only as an application-pattern reference. |
   | State-machine/reducer example | Detailed example | No dedicated reference found | Useful only as a state-modeling reference. |
   | Type-level equality/expected-error test helpers | Dedicated section | Manifest asks for tests, but no linked type-test reference | Useful advanced-types-only material; preserve as a concise type-testing reference. |
   | Performance limits for recursive/conditional types | Brief section | Not surfaced by linked rules | Useful advanced-types-only caution; add to an appropriate type-level rule, not the main workflow. |

   1. inspect `package.json`, workspace layout, and `tsconfig*.json` (or ask when unavailable) and select the narrowest project-native typecheck command;
   2. run that command and record the relevant errors;
   3. locate the root cause and load only the relevant `rules/*.md` link(s);
   4. implement the smallest sound type change, using `unknown`/narrowing at untrusted boundaries and retaining a documented intentional `any` only where it is the correct boundary;
   5. rerun the same typecheck command and any focused existing test/type-test command.

   Retain the present explicit rule index. Make explanations, alternatives, and type tests conditional: provide them when requested, when changing public/reusable type APIs, or when the project has an established type-test harness.

2. **Preserve only genuine old-skill gaps as disclosed references.** Add a compact `rules/type-tests.md` (equality assertions plus `@ts-expect-error`, with the project’s existing harness when present) and add a short complexity/recursion caution to `conditional-types.md` or `mapped-types.md`. Add an `application-patterns` reference only if API-client, form-validation, and reducer/state-machine designs are supported use cases; otherwise retire those tutorial examples. Only after that proof, remove `vendor-auto/typescript-advanced-types` (preferred) or move it to `vendor/` with a minimal user-invoked compatibility pointer that delegates to magician and does not repeat triggers. A pointer remaining in `vendor-auto` would violate the one-model-invoked-owner acceptance criterion.
